correctness.rationale: For either Laurent polynomial and n=5q+d, its dth power has exponents in [-4,4], so the product with a polynomial in x^5 has constant term only from two zero exponents. Frobenius therefore gives exact digit multiplication modulo five. The direct residues give the increments (0,0),(0,1),(3,1),(1,1),(2,0), so all n have nonzero residues and a padded length-L word is one of 5^L equally counted words. Convolution on (Z/4Z)^2 diagonalizes with the four rows 2+3i^s, i^s, 2−i^s, i^s. Inversion gives the table including L=0. For the differences of opposite rows only odd r contribute: they cancel for rows 1 and 3, and sum to the character delta at f=L mod 4 for rows 0 and 2. At L=3, f=0 requires zero second-coordinate increments, so first coordinates are even; for f=1 and f=2 there is a spare digit giving increment 2 if needed, and for f=3 choosing three first coordinates from {0,1,3} spans all four. At L=4 both missing cells occur, and zero padding preserves all cells. Adding high digit 4 in pairs creates infinitely many distinct indices with each unchanged pair. Projection off the marginals kills modes with r=0 or s=0; the nine remaining squared magnitudes are 9 once, 5 twice and 1 six times. Parseval gives (3); the (2,2) mode yields the 3^L checkerboard, with the remaining absolute amplitudes bounded as in (4). The full-table energy uses additionally 13 twice and 1 four times after removal of the constant, consistent with (8). The (2,0),(0,2),(2,2) modes give 1, (−1)^L, 3^L; dividing by block length and subtracting the product of the means gives the stated covariance. Direct sparse Laurent multiplication, not the digit recurrence, recovered the L=3 missing pair positions and all L=4 cells (minimum count 16, cross sum 81), via python3 /workspace/branches/independent-reproduction/arithmetic_review.py. Frozen checker inspected, not executed; the finite replay is corroboration.
